finding: Attack-labelled readings are not uniformly extreme
evidence: highest separation: weather/pressure with 26.4% of attack rows beyond 3 SD of the normal baseline; median across sensor-measures is 0.0%
interpretation: Simple threshold alarms on sensor values alone would miss most attack-labelled traffic, which is the argument for the learned models in steps 5 and 6.

finding: Connection state separates attack-labelled traffic strongly
evidence: state 'rej' carries 44,852 flows of which 100.0% are attack-labelled
interpretation: Half-open and rejected connections are the fingerprint of scanning and flooding; this is why conn_state is kept as a model feature.

finding: A small number of user-days break the behavioural baseline
evidence: 45 of 2792 user-days (1.6%) show either >= 3 failed logins, more than one source country, or any non-domestic source address; the 99th percentile of daily failures is 2.0
interpretation: These are candidates for investigation, not confirmed incidents. They are used in step 7 as the rule-based comparison for the machine-learning anomaly scores.

evidence: 2.01% of all access events are failures (455 of 22,686)
interpretation: This is the reference level any alerting threshold has to beat; a rule that fires on single failures would generate roughly 455 alerts a month.
